newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir party members fined for storming meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir party members fined for storming meeting.

text.p: A Malaysian court on Friday fined three members of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's political party for breaking up a conference on East Timor last November.

"We're fully responsible for our actions and I think we've paid our dues," Hishamuddin Hussein, spokesman for the trio and deputy youth chief for Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), told reporters.

The magistrate's court fined Nadzri Ismail, Mohamad Supardi Mohamad Noor and Abdul Hadi Mohamad Zam, all youth members of UMNO, 1,500 ringgit ($602) each for "trespassing and rioting" at the November 9 meeting.
A fourth UMNO youth member, Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, would face similar charges when he returned to Kuala Lumpur from an overseas mission next month, court officials said.

The four were part of about 100 youth members of Malaysia's ruling National Front coalition who stormed into the Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor II (Apcet II) at a hotel here and hurled chairs and tables to break up the meeting. UMNO, which heads the National Front, said the youths acted on their own to disrupt the meeting, which the government earlier tried to prevent to protect its good relations with Indonesia.
"We made our decision based on the circumstances then... we've no regret on that," said Hishamuddin, who spoke on behalf of those fined and UMNO Youth, outside the court house.

Police detained more than 100 people, including the conference participants and journalists, after the commotion at the meeting. Most were released unconditionally, while 60 who were let off on bail were told they would not be charged.
Malaysia deported 46 foreign participants after the aborted conference.
The Malaysian government feared the meeting would harm ties with Indonesia, which invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year, a move never recognised by the United Nations.
